text: Patience is to faith what the head is to the body — without it, there is no faith at all.
The heart that is truly attached to Allah finds a rest that nothing in this world can give it.
Knowledge without action is like a tree that bears no fruit.
The wound is the place where the light enters you.
Patience is bitter to taste, but what grows from it is sweeter than honey.
Do good quietly, and let the deed speak for you instead of your tongue.
This world is three days: yesterday, which has left you and will not return; today, which is yours, so use it well; and tomorrow, which you may never see.
Do not delay repentance out of false hope, and do not despair of mercy out of grief.
A moment of patience in a moment of anger saves a thousand moments of regret.
A grateful heart is a heart at peace, whatever it holds.
A person is known by the company he keeps — so choose your companions with care.
Leaving a sin for the sake of Allah is dearer to Him than many long nights of extra prayer.
Sincerity is the hardest thing to hold onto, because the heart keeps turning.
Do not lose yourself trying to please everyone; you were created to please your Lord.
The believer's affair is admirable — every matter of his is good, and this applies to no one but him.
ref: Adapted from a saying preserved by Imam Muslim

text: Whoever fears Allah, Allah teaches him what he did not know before.
The heart is like a mirror — sins are the rust that dulls it, and remembrance is the polish.
Whoever plants goodness lives to see its harvest, sooner or later.
Trials are the fire that separates true gold from mere metal.
Speak only when your words are more beautiful than your silence.
The one who forgives when able is greater in reward than the one who is never wronged.
A little that is enough is better than a lot that distracts.
Gratitude turns what we have into enough.
Ease is not the absence of hardship, but the presence of Allah within it.
The tongue of a wise man is behind his heart; the heart of a fool is behind his tongue.
